license_boundary.preferred_integration_shape: P2P -> vendor adapter / capability projection -> isolated OpenMontage source/runtime -> durable artifacts -> P2P ReturnPacket/evidence
license_boundary.reasoning: AGPL-3.0 is network-copyleft. P2P core cannot casually import, adapt, or snapshot OpenMontage implementation code without engaging AGPL obligations. Fail-closed choice: do not vendor source; keep a pinned reference-only record (URL, commit, tree, license pointer) in P2P; any future runtime invocation happens in an isolated external checkout/container owned by OpenMontage, not in P2P core.
license_boundary.legal_claim_scope: This record states license facts observed upstream only. It makes no legal opinion beyond the license text and does not assert compatibility with P2P core licensing.

vendor_classification.rationale: Uses existing canonical P2P vocabulary (registry mode PINNED_REFERENCE_ADAPTER as used by p2p-uiux; semantic kind EXTERNAL_RUNTIME and dependency mode EXTERNAL_RUNTIME_NOT_INSTALLED as used by img2threejs/majid records). No new vendor framework, registry, scheduler, orchestrator, provenance store, or governance ontology was created. LOCAL_VENDOR_SNAPSHOT was rejected because no AGPL source is snapshotted.

architecture.shape: agent-first (no code orchestrator): pipeline YAML manifests + Markdown director skills + Python tool registry; the host coding agent is the orchestrator
architecture.p2p_authority_boundary: P2P remains authority/orchestrator. OpenMontage is a bounded external production capability provider. P2P retains Control Tower, Work Factory, risk lanes, capability routing, ReturnPacket, Supervisor, Owner Gate. OpenMontage's internal pipeline/orchestration concepts are not imported as a second P2P authority layer.
authority_retained_by_p2p: bounded P2P work item -> OpenMontage adapter -> durable artifacts/evidence

security_assessment.scope: static surface inventory only; no execution, no broad security research
security_assessment.install_footprint: large: Python requirements + pip optional extras + Node (Remotion, HyperFrames via npx), FFmpeg, optional GPU stack
security_assessment.subprocess_usage: 50 subprocess invocations across 23 tool/lib/script files (FFmpeg, Node/npx, git/pip surfaces)
security_assessment.network_access: 67 tool/lib files use HTTP clients; provider calls are per-tool and key-gated; archive/stock ingestion is outbound
security_assessment.api_key_handling: dotenv (.env), 23+ env vars documented; no hardcoded keys found in scanned source; keys never stored in repo (.env ignored)
security_assessment.arbitrary_command_or_code_surfaces: high: 12 of 13 pipeline manifests set extensions.custom_scripts=true and custom_skills=true; agentic operation means the host AI agent executes scripts by design
security_assessment.downloads: 99 tool/lib files reference download surfaces (first-run model weights, Piper voice models, ComfyUI workflows, stock/archive media)
security_assessment.output_paths: default OPENMONTAGE_PROJECTS_DIR or <repo>/projects/<project>/renders/final.mp4 + hyperframes workspaces; checkpoints under pipeline storage dir; all overridable via env/config
security_assessment.provider_fallback: scored 7-dimension selector with documented fall-through (e.g. Remotion -> FFmpeg Ken Burns when Remotion unavailable); budget cap and per-action approval for paid tools
security_assessment.local_gpu_requirements: NVIDIA CUDA + torch stack; 6-24GB VRAM by model; documented NVML driver note and bf16/int8/int4 precision + offload modes
security_assessment.disk_requirements: multi-GB for local models; ~161MB repo clone; Remotion/Node deps
security_assessment.fail_closed_policy_for_p2p: vendor starts as REFERENCE_ONLY_EXTERNAL_RUNTIME_VENDOR; no P2P code, no adapter execution, no installs, no keys, no rendering
